# funSmooth

Function to smooth the values estimated by summary functions and create functional object to use during FDA

```{r}
#| label: function-funSmooth

#' fsmooth Function to convert a vector of data points into a continuous functional object 
#' It need a column to be the vector of r values, named "r_values"
#' 
#' @param df object of class data.frame or data.table
#' @param M spline order (norder)
#' @param genLfun.fd Lfdobj for fdPar
#' @param centered center by r before smoothing
#' @param nbasis allow user to set number of basis functions
#' @param breaks provide a coarser breaks vector
#' @param lambda smoothing penalty; if NULL a default is chosen
#' @param rangeval override range(r) if desired
#' @param verbose verbose true or false
#' @param ... other arguments for smooth.basis function
#' @importFrom fda create.bspline.basis fdPar smooth.basis
#' @return A list with the fd objects and the original matrix and r vector
#' @export

funSmooth <- function(
  df,
  M = 6,                  # spline order (norder)
  genLfun.fd = 4,         # Lfdobj for fdPar
  r_value = NULL,         # vector of r values
  centered = FALSE,       # center by r before smoothing
  nbasis = NULL,          # allow user to set number of basis functions
  breaks = NULL,          # alternative: provide a coarser breaks vector
  lambda = NULL,          # smoothing penalty; if NULL a default is chosen
  rangeval = NULL,        # override range(r) if desired
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
) {
  # 1. Robustly extract r
  rvals <- if (is.null(r_value)) "r_value" else r_value
  if (!rvals %in% names(df)) {
    if (verbose) message("Warning: colonna '", rvals, "' non trovata")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  r <- df[[rvals]]
  
  # 2. Extract functional matrix (all columns other then r_values)
  mat_fun <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(df)[setdiff(names(df), rvals)])
  if (is.null(colnames(mat_fun))) {
    colnames(mat_fun) <- paste0("S", seq_len(ncol(mat_fun)))
  }

  # 3. Optional centering
  if (isTRUE(centered)) {
    mat_fun <- sweep(mat_fun, MARGIN = 1, STATS = r, FUN = "-")
  }

  # 4. Determine range
  if (is.null(rangeval)) rangeval <- range(r, na.rm = TRUE)

  # 5. Choose nbasis sensibly if not provided
  n_r <- length(r)
  if (!is.null(breaks)) {
    # If the user supplied breaks, follow fda convention
    nbasis_calc <- length(breaks) + M - 2
    if (verbose) message("Using user-supplied breaks; nbasis computed as: ", nbasis_calc)
    genbasis <- create.bspline.basis(rangeval = rangeval, nbasis = nbasis_calc, norder = M, breaks = breaks)
  } else {
    if (!is.null(nbasis)) {
      nbasis_calc <- nbasis
    } else {
      # default heuristic: up to 30 bases but not larger than roughly n_r/4
      nbasis_calc <- min(30, max(M + 1, floor(n_r / 4)))
    }
    if (nbasis_calc >= n_r) {
      if (verbose) message("nbasis (", nbasis_calc, ") >= number of observations (", n_r, "); reducing nbasis to avoid overparameterization")
      nbasis_calc <- max(M + 1, n_r - 1)
    }
    genbasis <- create.bspline.basis(rangeval = rangeval, nbasis = nbasis_calc, norder = M)
  }

  # 6. Choose lambda if not provided (avoid near-interpolation)
  if (is.null(lambda)) {
    # A conservative default that provides some smoothing; users may increase
    # but avoid values like 1e-11 which effectively disable penalization
    lambda_val <- 1e-6
  } else {
    lambda_val <- lambda
  }

  genfdPar <- fdPar(genbasis, genLfun.fd, lambda = lambda_val)

  # 7. Try smoothing with fallback strategies on error
  genfdSmooth <- tryCatch(
    smooth.basis(argvals = r, y = mat_fun, fdParobj = genfdPar, ...),
    error = function(e) {
      if (verbose) message("smooth.basis failed: ", conditionMessage(e), "; retrying with larger lambda and Lfdobj=2")
      # fallback: increase penalty and use Lfdobj=2
      tryCatch(
        {
          genfdPar2 <- fdPar(genbasis, Lfdobj = 2, lambda = max(lambda_val, 1e-4))
          smooth.basis(argvals = r, y = mat_fun, fdParobj = genfdPar2, ...)
        },
        error = function(e2) {
          stop("Both primary and fallback smoothing attempts failed: ", conditionMessage(e2))
        }
      )
    }
  )

  Genfun.fd <- genfdSmooth$fd

  # 8. Set names defensively
  fdn_dist <- paste("Distance (from 0 to", max(r, na.rm = TRUE), "micron)")
  fdnames <- list(fdn_dist,
                  "Sample" = colnames(mat_fun),
                  "Function")
  Genfun.fd$fdnames <- fdnames

  # 9. Basic sanity checks
  if (!is.null(Genfun.fd$coefs)) {
    n_coefs <- ncol(Genfun.fd$coefs)
    if (ncol(mat_fun) != n_coefs) {
      if (verbose) message("Warning: number of functions in mat_fun (", ncol(mat_fun), ") != number of fd coefficient columns (", n_coefs, ")")
    } else {
      if (verbose) message("Finished smoothing: nbasis=", genbasis$nbasis, ", lambda=", lambda_val)
    }
  } else {
    if (verbose) message("Finished smoothing but fd$coefs is NULL")
  }

  return(list(fd = Genfun.fd, fdPar = genfdPar, basis = genbasis, mat = mat_fun, r = r))
}
```

## Lambda selection

Helper function to select optimal lambda through GCV and Degrees of freedom

In ingresso ha mat_fun, r, basis, Lfdobj

```{r}
#| label: function-lambdaRamsay

#' Function to estimate optimal lambda
#' 
#' @param matV matrix with values of summary function, one sample for each column
#' @param rValues vector "r" of values for which the summary functions are evaluated
#' @param sBasis Bspline basis
#' @param Lfd max value of differentiation 
#' @param nGrid length of the grid to evaluate lambda on
#' @param dfRange range of lambda values to be evaluated
lambdaRamsay <- function(matV, rValues, sBasis, Lfd, 
                         nGrid = 50,
                         dfRange= c(2.5, 0.5 * length(rValues)))
{
  # control to avoid a not achievable target
  stopifnot(dfRange[1] > Lfd)
  Lfdobj <- int2Lfd(Lfd)
  
  ll_min <- find_loglam(dfRange[2])   # lambda piccolo -> df alti (poco liscio)
  ll_max <- find_loglam(dfRange[1])   # lambda grande  -> df bassi (quasi retta)
# 3. GCV su griglia
  grid <- seq(ll_min, ll_max, length.out = nGrid)
  tab  <- as.data.frame(t(sapply(grid, function(ll) {
    sm <- genfdSmoother(loglam = ll, y = matV, basis = sBasis, 
                        Lfdb = Lfdobj, tt = rValues)
    c(loglam = ll, df = sm$df, gcv = sum(sm$gcv))
  })))

  i <- which.min(tab$gcv)
  if (i %in% c(1, nGrid)) {
    warning("Minimo GCV sul bordo del range: considera di allargare df_range")
  }

  # 4. Raffinamento locale attorno al minimo
  opt <- optimize(function(ll) sum(genfdSmoother(loglam = ll, y = matV, basis = sBasis, 
                        Lfdb = Lfdobj, tt = rValues)$gcv),
                  interval = c(tab$loglam[max(i - 1, 1)], 
                               tab$loglam[min(i + 1, nGrid)]))
  best <- genfdSmoother(opt$minimum)

  list(
    lambda = 10^opt$minimum,
    df     = best$df,
    gcv    = sum(best$gcv),
    fd     = best$fd,
    basis  = basis,
    table  = tab
  )
}
```

## Helper functions

```{r}

genfdSmoother <- function(loglam, y, basis, Lfdb, tt) {
  smooth.basis(tt, y, fdPar(basis, Lfdobj, 10^loglam))
}
  
# i df dipendono solo da lambda e dalle basi, non dai dati: basta una curva
df_of <- function(loglam) fit(loglam, Y[, 1])$df
  
# 2. range di lambda ricavato dai gradi di liberta' (df decresce con lambda)
find_loglam <- function(target)
    uniroot(function(ll) df_of(ll) - target, c(-12, 8), extendInt = "yes")$root
```
